title: Platinum complexes as inhibitors of DNA repair protein Ku70 and topoisomerase IIalpha in cancer cells.
authors: Zhang, Hongmei; Wang, Ying; Wang, Yanqing; Han, Qianqian; Yan, Honghao; Yang, Tao; Guo, Zijian; Wang, Xiaoyong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究铂配合物抑制DNA修复蛋白Ku70和拓扑异构酶IIα的抗癌机制，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作和分子对接，但核心是药物设计与细胞实验，非TF-DNA结合建模，方法深度有限。
abstract: Ku70 protein and topoisomerase IIalpha (Topo IIalpha) are promising targets of anticancer drugs, which play critical roles in DNA repair and replication processes. Three platinum(II) complexes, [PtCl(NH(3))(2)(9-(pyridin-2-ylmethyl)-9H-carbazole)]NO(3) (OPPC), [PtCl(NH(3))(2)(9-(pyridin-3-ylmethyl)-9H-carbazole)]NO(3) (MPPC), and [PtCl(NH(3))(2)(9-(pyridin-4-ylmethyl)-9H-carbazole)]NO(3) (PPPC), were designed as inhibitors of Ku70 and Topo IIalpha. Their antitumor activity and inhibitory efficacy on Ku70 and Topo IIalpha were investigated on cellular and molecular levels. OPPC exhibited high antiproliferative activity against various cancer cell lines, with acute toxicity to mice being lower than that of cisplatin. Moreover, OPPC could enter cancer cells effectively and cause DNA damage, which was evidenced by the enhanced expression of gamma-H2AX, Chk1/2 phosphorylation, p53 and cell cycle arrest. OPPC also downregulated the DNA damage repair protein Ku70 and inhibited the formation of Ku70 foci-the central points or loci of Ku70, which would suppress DNA repair and induce a nonhomologous end joining response in cancer cells. More importantly, these complexes showed inhibition towards Topo IIalpha; in particular, OPPC was more effective than MPPC and PPPC. In the Topo IIalpha knockdown cells, Ku70 and Topo IIalpha were directly associated with the DNA damage and apoptotic response. The molecular docking provided detailed structural insights into the interactions of the complexes with Topo IIalpha. This study demonstrates that the cytotoxicity of these complexes is associated with the DNA damage and repair pathways mediated by Ku70 and Topo IIalpha; OPPC is an effective inhibitor of Ku70 and Topo IIalpha and restrains cancer cells via a mechanism utterly distinct from that of cisplatin.
abstract_zh: Ku70蛋白和拓扑异构酶IIα（Topo IIα）是抗癌药物的有前景靶点，在DNA修复和复制过程中发挥关键作用。设计并合成了三种铂(II)配合物，[PtCl(NH(3))(2)(9-(吡啶-2-基甲基)-9H-咔唑)]NO(3) (OPPC)、[PtCl(NH(3))(2)(9-(吡啶-3-基甲基)-9H-咔唑)]NO(3) (MPPC)和[PtCl(NH(3))(2)(9-(吡啶-4-基甲基)-9H-咔唑)]NO(3) (PPPC)，作为Ku70和Topo IIα的抑制剂。在细胞和分子水平上研究了它们的抗肿瘤活性及对Ku70和Topo IIα的抑制效果。OPPC对多种癌细胞系表现出高抗增殖活性，且对小鼠的急性毒性低于顺铂。此外，OPPC能有效进入癌细胞并引起DNA损伤，这通过γ-H2AX表达增强、Chk1/2磷酸化、p53上调及细胞周期阻滞得到证实。OPPC还下调DNA损伤修复蛋白Ku70并抑制Ku70焦点（Ku70的中心点或位点）的形成，这将抑制DNA修复并诱导癌细胞中的非同源末端连接反应。更重要的是，这些配合物对Topo IIα表现出抑制作用；特别是，OPPC比MPPC和PPPC更有效。在Topo IIα敲低细胞中，Ku70和Topo IIα直接与DNA损伤和凋亡反应相关。分子对接提供了配合物与Topo IIα相互作用的详细结构见解。本研究证明，这些配合物的细胞毒性与其通过Ku70和Topo IIα介导的DNA损伤和修复途径相关；OPPC是Ku70和Topo IIα的有效抑制剂，并通过与顺铂完全不同的机制抑制癌细胞。
